title: Marketing for Construction Companies: Scale Past £1M
meta_description: Marketing for construction companies turning over £1M+ needs a strategy, not luck. How to attract high-value clients and scale with proven methods.
h1: Marketing for Construction Companies: Scale Past £1M
hero_subtitle: A practical guide for businesses already at £1M and working harder for thinner margins.

intro.answer: Scaling from £1 million to £5 million is not about working harder on site. It is about working smarter off it, moving from reactive bidding to marketing that targets the clients you actually want.

image.alt: A construction company owner planning the marketing that scales the business past £1M

intro.roadmap: This guide follows the five stages: understanding the competitive landscape, attracting the right leads through your digital presence and outbound work, converting them without discounting, delivering so well that delivery becomes marketing, and scaling with a team.

briefing.title: Know Who You Are Actually Competing With
briefing.intro: The construction industry is traditionally slow to adopt modern business practice, which is exactly why it stays a large opportunity for the businesses that do. But nothing works until you know the real competition, and most owners get that wrong.

panels.heading: Who are you really competing against?
paragraphs: Most owners assume it is the other local builders of roughly their size. Often it is not. On the work worth having you are up against a different set of companies entirely, sometimes larger, sometimes from an adjacent sector.
Work that out before you spend a penny on ads or content, because it changes the message, the channel and the price you can hold.

panels.heading: Then work the five stages in order
paragraphs: Each stage assumes the one before it is done. Skipping ahead is why marketing budgets disappear without result.
steps: Plan: understand the competitive landscape and where you genuinely win.
Attract: a professional digital presence, social media used for relationships, and outbound that reaches decision makers.
Convert: a sales funnel, and a way of handling price objections that does not end in a discount.
Deliver: systems, processes and cash flow management, because delivery is marketing.
Scale: hiring, retention, delegation and continuous improvement.

review.label: Worth knowing
review.text: The frustrations at £1M are consistent: cash flow gaps, the hunt for skilled labour, and working harder than your subcontractors for thinner margins. None of those are fixed by winning more of the same work.
